<includeonly><span id="{{{1|}}}"></span></includeonly><noinclude>
'''Usage:''' <code><nowiki>{{anchor|Anchor_name}}</nowiki></code> creates the link target <code>#Anchor_name</code> on the current page.

'''Every heading already gets a link target automatically.''' A heading that mixes text and math is normalised: the <code>$…$</code> math is dropped (a heading that is ONLY math keeps it), and the characters that cannot appear in a fragment — <code># &lt; &gt; [ ] | { }</code> — become <code>_</code>. So this needs no template call:

<code><nowiki>=== Symmetric groups $\mathcal{S}_{n}$ ===</nowiki></code> → <code><nowiki>[[Page#Symmetric_groups]]</nowiki></code>

The section's <code>[Copy internal mention]</code> and <code>[Copy URL]</code> use that anchor.

Use this template when you want a different, readable anchor — especially for a math-only heading or a long heading. It '''wins''' over the automatic anchor:

<code><nowiki>=== {{anchor|sign composition}} $\operatorname{sign}(\sigma_1 \circ \sigma_2)$ ===</nowiki></code> → <code><nowiki>[[Permutation#sign composition]]</nowiki></code>

The anchor must not contain any of <code># &lt; &gt; [ ] | { }</code>; prefer <code>_</code> instead of spaces (the automatic anchors use it). This wiki does not have ParserFunctions, so there is no multi-anchor form: call the template once per anchor.

Place the call at the start of the heading (<code>=== <nowiki>{{anchor|Name}}</nowiki>Heading ===</code>) or at the start of the section body on the same line as the text. A call alone on its own line produces an empty paragraph.
</noinclude>
